deep.reconstruction:
This is a page of pure numerical work (folio 131, headed 'Litt. C', old number 169 struck out) belonging to a Gauss orbit determination of 1805, almost certainly for a newly found minor planet, using four geocentric observations (the previous page lists sun longitudes l, l', l'', l''' and angles alpha, alpha', ... with R, cos b, sin(l-alpha) style quantities). The page contains no prose or symbolic derivation; the purpose of each block has to be inferred from the labels (R', R'', cos b', cos b'', sin(l-alpha), Csin = logarithmic complement of a sine, 'Pars const.', 'Coeff Pars', P', Q', c', d', 'Hieraus x', x''') and from the numbers. My reading is therefore partly inferential.

Block 1 (top left): two columns of logarithmic computations (one for each of two unknown-coefficient equations). Each starts from log R (0.0038571 and 0.0065812, i.e. the earlier tabulated sun-distance quantities), adds log cos b and log sin(l-alpha), and the complement-log of sin(alpha-alpha). Summing gives logarithms 0.8975955n / 0.7131598n, converted to numbers -7.8994255 / -5.1660643, and then -0.6515199 / -0.2084252. A second group (-R''/cos b'') gives +36.849051 and +2.3859884, which are combined with the previous terms to give the 'constant part' 37.500571 / 2.5944136 (crossed out, then replaced by the boxed corrected values 37.057476 and 3.0375083, obtained as 36.849051+0.208425 and 2.3859884+0.6515199: the first pass had added the wrong cross-term, and the cross is visible in the image). Reading of structure: these are the constant (non-iterated) parts of two linear equations for the two unknown distance-like quantities.

Block 2: log Coeff Pars = 0.8373995 / 0.6182547, then adding log P' (0.0027955 / 9.9886858) gives 6.9214175 / 4.0452046 (log of the P-dependent part, the number 6.921417 and 4.0452046 are used directly as numbers in the sum below). Then sin(alpha''-alpha), Csin(alpha'-alpha), cos b'/cos b'' give log 0.5177015 / 9.8776847; adding 1+P' (0.3024295 / 0.2954097) gives log d' = 0.8201310 / 0.1730944 (the first-written 0.8203310 is overwritten). Then c' = 37.057476 + 6.921417 = 43.978893 (the first attempts 43.9776623 and 44.421988 are struck out), and 3.0375083 + 4.0452046 = 7.0827129.

Block 3 (centre): 'Hieraus x' = 2.0969, x'' = 1.9726' as a first rough reading, then refined: x' = c' - d' * (something) = 43.978893 - 42.005320 = 1.9735738 and 7.0827129 - 4.9848109 = 2.0979020. The columns of logs 8.5509454 (log a' related, b' = -8.5509454) and 5.3744895 (b''=-5.3744895 from previous page) are subtracted from 6.4530434 / 3.4009157 and so on, turning logarithms into the numbers 42.005320 and 4.9848109. So the unknowns x', x'' are obtained as differences of large nearly equal quantities, which is why 7-figure logarithms are needed.

Block 4 (centre-left, boxed): the check sum 36.849051+0.208425=37.057476 and 2.385988+0.651520=3.037508, then log sums 9.2572108, 0.3492520, 0.3443132 and 9.6064628 / 9.6015240. Subtracting 9.9886858 and 0.0027955 (log P'' and log P') gives 0.2930427 / 0.2996823. Further lines give 9.5987285 / 9.6177770 and so on down to angles 18 deg 25' 17.75'' and 17 deg 29' 41.71'' and 5 deg 12' 29.99''. These angle-valued quantities look like the unknown eccentric-anomaly-type differences (or half sector angles) found by trial; three trial values 10 deg 5' 50'', 10 24 59.98, 10 55 16.05 are tabulated with logs 0.3548982, 0.3492520, 0.3443132, 0.3402653.

Block 5 (bottom centre): a three-column trial computation at arguments 5.2.55.055, 5.12.29.99, 5.27.38.025 (and halves 2.31.27.5275, 2.36.14.995, 2.43.49.0125) with logs 8.6438801 / 8.6573964 / 8.6779204 and 7.2877602 etc., and final numbers 19473.7, 20729.5, 22793.8 with differences 106.1, 81.2, 54.5 and 8333333.3 (= 10^8/12). Number 8333333.3 = 1/120 * 10^9 or 10^8/12: this looks like the coefficient of a series expansion of the sine/sector-triangle ratio (the term 1/12, 1/120). So this is the series evaluation of the function relating the sector-to-triangle ratio to the angle, tabulated at three values for interpolation. Closeness to the method later published in Theoria Motus (Book II, section on determining the orbit from four observations / the equations with P and Q) is strong but not proven from this page alone.

Block 6 (right): second iteration of x' and x'' with x'' = 1.9735738 first trial (and 1.9735596 struck out), 5.3744895 - 3.4009157 etc., result x' = 2.0979020 again and 4.9848109. The right-hand columns recompute 9.8866898 / 9.9972313 (log a', a'') with 0.3217852 / 0.2952533, giving 9.9725332 / 9.9509401, then with log Q' = 9.2322405 and log Q'' = 9.2463502 produce 1.0477560 and 1.0329396. Angle arithmetic 20.9.47.94, 26.43.26.83, minus 14.57.24.81 and 11.11.10.24, then differences -5.12.23.13, -15.32.16.59, -10.22.19.86 and +5.9.56.73 appear; the value 5.12.29.99 and 10.24.59.98 (twice 5.12.29.99) are carried to the middle columns. Further logs of sines (9.2553729n, 8.8703566, ... -8 deg 27'41.89'') are used for a correction angle. The bottom right gives a third interpolation table (0.3520751, 0.3467826, 0.3422892 etc., logs 9.5304750, 1.9542507, 7.5762243, 9.9218380, 45.1218 / 47.4369 / 51.6006, 0.0043202 / 0.0045400 / 0.0049349) and the revised values log P' = 0.0026856, log P'' = 9.9888832, log Q' = 9.2375845, log Q'' = 9.2520671, which feed into the next page (Litt. Q, folio 176 in the transcription), where the same pattern is repeated with these values.

Overall: successive approximation of the two unknown quantities x', x'' (about 2.0979 and 1.9736 at this stage), with P', P'', Q', Q'' updated each pass, using logarithm tables and a series evaluation tabulated at three trial arguments for interpolation. It is routine hand calculation for the orbit of a minor planet (Ceres, Pallas or Juno era, 1805).
errors: The first 'Pars const.' entries 37.500571 and 2.5944136 are crossed out in the manuscript and replaced by 37.057476 and 3.0375083; Gauss corrected them himself.

Several first-written values are struck out and corrected (c' = 43.9776623 and 44.421988 replaced by 43.978893; x'' = 1.9735596 replaced by 1.9735738; log d' first written 0.8203310, corrected to 0.8201310; 0.0048401 replaced by 0.0049349). Self-corrections, not errors in the final numbers.

I have not independently recomputed the logarithms; the structure of the unknowns (what x', x'' are, what Q represents) is an inference, not stated on the page. The reading of 8333333.3 as a 1/12 coefficient is a guess.
